$comment: DR-15/R2-M5 MACHINE-READABLE CIPHER-SUITE REGISTRY — the versioned preference vector AND the MANDATORY FLOOR, in one place, owned by the federation design authority (umbrella §13.4). The floor is a versioned CONSTANT rather than a number in prose precisely so that raising it is a GOVERNANCE action with an audit trail, not an edit. Before this file the profile said a member MAY refuse a suite below its 'locally configured floor': optional, unpublished, unverifiable, and ambiguous because the same advertised list also contains the mandatory baseline. A floor each participant declares protects only the participants who declare one — and a member that publishes nothing is exactly where a provider-induced downgrade lands.

preference_vector.$comment: Strongest-first total order. Deterministic selection (N3): two conforming creators pick the same suite from the same capability sets. Post-quantum resistance ranks first (harvest-now-decrypt-later), then classical margin, then hardware-holdability, then the baseline.

floor.$comment: MANDATORY, binding on EVERY conforming deployment including one that publishes nothing, and evaluable with no discovery fetch — so two creators with the same capability sets always reach the same decision. Set at the BASELINE deliberately: the baseline is REQUIRED of every implementation and ranks LAST in the preference vector, so a floor here adds no cryptographic STRENGTH — it adds uniform ENFORCEMENT, which is what was missing ('MAY refuse' becomes 'MUST NOT form'). Setting it at the hardware-holdable P-256 was considered and rejected: it would exclude software-only wallets and break the invariant that the baseline is in every intersection, so a selection always exists — a new requirement DR-15 does not ask for. A device MAY publish a HIGHER floor (BW-MEMBER 2.2 `min_cipher_suite`); it may never publish a lower one.
